newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU to tie GAN clearance to 1998 selloff -paper.
newsitem.headline: EU to tie GAN clearance to 1998 selloff -paper.

text.p: The European Commission will approve French government aid to the state-owned insurer GAN on Wednesday in return for a pledge to privatise it by mid-1998, business daily Les Echos said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the Commission would approve a state aid package worth around 20 billion francs in return for the pledge to privatise both GAN and its banking subsidiary CIC.
Another condition tied to the state aid approval would be that GAN had to divest half of its network outside France in the 12 months following privatisation.
The new Socialist-led government said in mid-July it would not go back on the previous centre-right government's plan to privatise GAN and CIC, or Credit Industriel et Commercial.

Commission sources said on Monday that the state aid package, which consists of a capital injection of 11 billion francs and a further nine billion to cover restructuring losses, would be approved at the Commission's weekly meeting on Wednesday.
